environment_pinning.issue: results/method_demo_synthetic.png as committed does not reproduce from the committed generator in a later environment: same canvas (1612x832), same dpi, and identical matplotlib (3.10.1 in the committed PNG's metadata and in the regenerating environment), but 1.59% of pixels differ across 491 connected components, 8 of them larger than 200 px -- solid-region change, not antialiasing. The generator is deterministic (numpy default_rng(seed=1)) and two consecutive runs are byte-identical, and no commit has touched analysis/ since the figure was committed, so the difference comes from a dependency version, not from the code or the seed.
environment_pinning.not_identified: Which dependency was NOT determined. matplotlib is ruled out by the PNG metadata. analysis/pyproject.toml pins only numpy>=1.24 and scipy>=1.10 with no upper bounds, so scipy.ndimage or numpy is the likely source, but this was not narrowed further and is not asserted.
environment_pinning.recommendation: Commit a small numeric artifact alongside the figure (candidate count and per-candidate geometry) so a future mismatch can be localised to a number rather than to pixels, and record the resolved dependency versions next to the figure.
